notes.note: Blocking is observed by timing: caller measures that the call returns only after the delayed reply (>=0.4 s); callee measures that getcall waits for the delayed call. Timing-based, tolerances of 0.1 s.
Timing-based: noblock call returns immediately (<0.2 s) on the caller side while the callee's getcall blocks until the call arrives (>=0.25 s).
Clause 13 rule tested: a noblock signature shall only have in parameters (inout parameter used).
Reading chosen: handling the exception is optional and a catch in an alt statement is one allowed way; test uses catch in alt.
Connections are dynamic, so addressing a non-connected component is detected at runtime; expected test case error.

Needs an SUT, hence noexecution. Titan warning is a Titan deviation: it requires its proprietary address extension and only accepts component references in to clauses; the module-level address type is standard (clause 6.2.9).

Needs an SUT, hence noexecution; reaching SUT entities shown via to/from clauses with the address type bound to the port type (6.2.9). Titan warning is a Titan deviation (no support for address declarations in port types).
Violation (send without to clause on a one-to-many connection) is only detectable at runtime; expected test case error.
Reading chosen: getcall stores in/inout parameters, getreply stores return value (and inout parameter), catch stores the exception.
Reading chosen: type compatibility instead of type identity suffices; a message of an integer subtype is stored into a plain integer variable.
